thread:
maria (PM): Quick heads-up — 3pm sync to align the onramp packaging + network ownership tradeoffs. Need clear launch criteria for the customer-managed networking path.
vik (Eng): +1. I'll bring the relay vs operator shim perf numbers.
leo (NetOps): high-level concerns: egress IP preservation, customer NATs, and BGP peering complexity. we can't promise static IPs unless they opt into 'preserve-egress' lane.
ashley (CS): customers asking for: preserved egress (banking), KMS/HSM integration, and an offline installer option for airgapped sites. also a simple rollback path.
maria (PM): goal for the meeting: decide lanes, minimal launch checklist, and who owns support for each lane.
vik (Eng): proposed lanes: 1) relay-mode (Redwood relay + nat traversal) — fastest ship, degraded latency but simplest for customers; 2) direct-peering (customer-managed VPC peering/BGP) — complex but lowest latency; 3) airgap/installer (offline bundle) — needs separate packaging/telemetry plan.
leo (NetOps): agree. direct-peering needs: public ASN, BGP sessions, route filters, IP preservation plan. also IPAM mapping doc.
ashley (CS): can we codify the customer commitments for direct-peering? like: maintain ASN, allow TCP/UDP ranges, preserve NAT translations. customers want that in the SOW.
maria (PM): yep. action: ashley to draft SOW checklist for each lane. vik to validate perf delta and slot estimates. leo to draft netops runbook for direct-peering.
vik (Eng): rough perf numbers from bench: relay-mode adds ~30–80ms median (depends on region), direct-peering ~+5–10ms, airgap varies. will attach microbench in the doc.
leo (NetOps): practical blocker: some customers can't change egress IPs. For relay-mode we can do `--preserve-egress-ip` when paired with a managed NAT; otherwise fallback.
maria (PM): launch criteria (draft):
- Lane definitions published + docs for customers
- SOW checklist per lane (ashley)
- Netops runbook + IPAM mapping template (leo)
- Installer parity for minimal inference (airgap)
- Metrics: latency budget, token throughput target, and rollback steps
- Support SLAs for dedicated vs hosted lanes
vik (Eng): add: operator must support pinning model version and auto-fallback to relay when peering fails.
leo (NetOps): will need an automated probe to detect peering health and fail traffic to relay; otherwise risk silent failures.
ashley (CS): CS asks that we include an onboarding checklist for netops teams (contact points, change window expectations, traceroute sample).
deploy-bot: meeting scheduled: 2024-06-21 15:00 UTC — <https://zoom.company/meeting/1234> :calendar: 
maria (PM): decision tentatively: ship relay-mode + docs first as GA, gate direct-peering to a beta with strict SOW. airgap is alpha with limited customers.
vik (Eng): timeline: prototype relay autoscale + failover in 2 weeks, direct-peering runbook + BGP tests in 4-6 weeks, airgap installer alpha in 6-8 weeks.
leo (NetOps): I'll circulate the route-filter template and ask the SREs to run a dry-run for BGP session setup.
ashley (CS): I'll pull customers who asked for preserved-egress and KMS into an early access program.
maria (PM): OK — final action items in the doc: Assign owners and due dates, we'll re-run at next Friday's product sync. :thumbsup:
vik (Eng): copying the checklist snippet for the relay config:```yaml
relay:
  enable: true
  preserve_egress: false # toggle for customers with NAT IPs
  failover: direct_peering
```
leo (NetOps): noted. small ask — include a test plan snippet for peering: `bgp-session-check`, `route-advertise-sanity`, `traceroute-verify`.
maria (PM): thanks everyone. I'll post the meeting notes + RFC link after the sync.
